title: docs(components): document `wrapperClass` and its new refusal on the five pages that omit it
body:
Fixes #8095

The docs half of objectui#7722, filed deliberately as a separate card. Schema declarations are untouched — they landed on PR objectui#8085 and this branch does not go near them.

## What changed

Five pages, 55 added lines, 0 removed:

| page | schema |
|---|---|
| `content/docs/components/form/switch.mdx` | `SwitchSchema` |
| `content/docs/components/form/textarea.mdx` | `TextareaSchema` |
| `content/docs/components/form/date-picker.mdx` | `DatePickerSchema` |
| `content/docs/components/form/select.mdx` | `SelectSchema` |
| `content/docs/components/data-display/list.mdx` | `ListSchema` |

Each page gets **two** things, because the second is the one this card exists for:

1. A `wrapperClass?: string;` row in the page's own interface block — the treatment `CheckboxSchema` landed with under objectui#6938 and `FilterBuilder` / `FileUpload` under objectui#6150. Each row matches **its own page's** shape (bare on the four pages whose blocks carry no trailing comments; under the existing `// Styling` group on `date-picker.mdx`) rather than importing one page's shape into another.
2. A warning callout — the same vehicle `combobox.mdx` already uses for a refusal note — saying that the key is now typed and that a **non-string** value which used to parse green is refused now. A bare row would have documented the member and hidden the behaviour change.

## The refusal, measured on this tree rather than restated

The card's load-bearing claim was measured on built artifacts either side of PR objectui#8085 during that card's tier review. It was cheap to re-measure the **after** half here, so it was: `pnpm --filter @object-ui/types build`, then a probe against `packages/types/dist/zod/index.zod.js`.

| probe | result |
|---|---|
| non-string `wrapperClass` on each of the five mirrors | `success=false`, one issue, `invalid_type` at path `wrapperClass` — all five |
| same node through `safeValidateSchema` | `success=false`, one issue, `invalid_type` at path `wrapperClass` — all five |
| **control** — a string `wrapperClass` on each mirror | `success=true` — all five, so the probe can pass |
| **passthrough proxy** — an undeclared key with a non-string value | `success=true` — all five |

Two honest limits on that reading:

- The **before** half is not re-measured here. Nobody built a pre-objectui#8085 artifact on this branch. The fourth row is a *proxy*: it shows the `.passthrough()` silence still in force for an undeclared key, which is the mechanism the card says `wrapperClass` itself enjoyed before it was declared. The claim that `wrapperClass` specifically parsed green then is the filing seat's measurement, cited as theirs.
- The card describes the `safeValidateSchema` symptom as "a root-level union issue". What the document parse actually surfaces is one issue at path `wrapperClass` with code `invalid_type` — named, not an opaque union failure. The pages say "refused by name", which is what was measured. The exact message string is deliberately not quoted into the docs, so the pages do not pin wording no consumer parses.

## The card's two other premises, re-derived on today's `main`

- **The five renderers do read the key.** `renderers/form/{switch,textarea,date-picker,select}.tsx` and `renderers/data-display/list.tsx` each interpolate `schema.wrapperClass` onto the wrapper element — five paths named, five hits, no miss. This is what makes the key a supported member to document rather than a feature to announce.
- **Five is still the right number.** Re-derived rather than trusted: the five paths exist, all five omitted the key, and no sixth page documents any of those five schemas (the census is over `interface NAMESchema` blocks in `content/` — one page each, with `FileUploadSchema`'s second hit being prose *about* the fence gate in `guide/ci-cd-pipeline.md`, not a schema page). The named risk — objectui#8072 growing the set by one — **has not landed**: `InputSchema`'s zod mirror still carries no `wrapperClass`, and a non-string there still parses `success=true`. So `input.mdx` is correctly out of scope; documenting the refusal there would describe a refusal that does not happen.

## Gates

Derived from objectui's own `package.json` scripts and `.github/workflows/`, because `scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs` refuses for objectui paths (exit 2). Each exit code captured on its own line into a file, never after a pipe.

| gate | exit |
|---|---|
| `check:doc-types` | 0 — 188 files, 1107 blocks, 900 type literals judged |
| `check:doc-fences` | 0 — 227 documents; the shrink-only baseline still reads 89 blocks across 80 files, so the five pages still carry one block each |
| `check:doc-example-ids` | 0 |
| `check:doc-example-readers` | 0 |
| `docs:check-links` | 0 |
| `check:docs-route-closure` | 0 |
| `check-doc-expression-carriage.mjs` | 0 |
| `check:control-bytes` | 0 |
| `check:new-line-citations` | 0 |
| `check:shell-escape-residue` | 0 |
| `check-changeset-presence.mjs` | 0 — its own verdict: 5 files changed, 0 of them published source of a released package, so **no changeset is owed**. The label is inert here; the gate decided |
| `check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` | 0 — NOT GOVERNED, ordinary review and merge-queue route |
| `check:doc-snippets` | see below |
| `check:doc-examples` | see below |

The last two are reported in the report body, not here as a pass — they exit 2 = PRECONDITION NOT MET without built packages, which is "could not run", not "ran and found nothing".

Repo-wide `pnpm lint` and `pnpm test` are CI's runs, not this branch's debt.

## Acceptance notes

Seen while measuring, deliberately **not** filed and **not** fixed here:

- `switch.mdx`, `textarea.mdx` and `select.mdx` document no `className` either, though every node carries it from `BaseSchema`. That is an omitted member with nothing refused behind it — the reading triage explicitly declined for this card — so it is an observation, not a finding. No successor: no queued card touches these three pages.
- `InputShorthandSchema` (the `email` / `password` shorthand) **does** declare `wrapperClass` on the zod face while `InputSchema` does not, so a non-string `wrapperClass` is refused under `type: email` and accepted under `type: input` today. That asymmetry belongs to objectui#8072's lane, which is named on the card as related-but-not-this. Noted so that lane does not have to re-measure it.
